'''Margaret Patricia O'Sullivan Pepe''' (born June 24, 1961) is an Irish biostatistician specializing in the evaluation of tests and biomarkers for disease screening. She is a professor of biostatistics at the [[University of Washington School of Public Health]] and a researcher at the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]].

== Life ==
Pepe was born June 24, 1961, in [[Cork (city)|Cork]], Ireland to Seamus O'Sullivan.<ref name=":1" /> She attended [[Mount Mercy College, Cork]].<ref name=":1" /> She completed a B.Sc. in mathematics science at the [[University College Cork]] in 1981.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Margaret Sullivan Pepe {{!}} Summer Institutes |url=https://si.biostat.washington.edu/people/margaret-pepe |access-date=2023-02-12 |website=si.biostat.washington.edu}}</ref> Pepe earned a M.S. in statistics in 1984 and a Ph.D. in biostatistics at the [[University of Washington School of Public Health]] in 1986.<ref name=":0" /> Her dissertation was titled, ''A new class of statistics for the two-sample survival analysis problem''.<ref name=":1">{{Cite thesis |last=O'Sullivan |first=Margaret Patricia |title=A new class of statistics for the two-sample survival analysis problem |date=1986 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=University of Washington |oclc=15155185}}</ref> [[Thomas R. Fleming]] was her doctoral advisor.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=25297}}</ref>

In 1997, she won the [[Mortimer Spiegelman Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Awards |url=https://www.apha.org/apha-communities/member-sections/applied-public-health-statistics/who-we-are/awards |access-date=2023-02-14 |website=www.apha.org |archive-date=2023-02-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230214033141/https://www.apha.org/apha-communities/member-sections/applied-public-health-statistics/who-we-are/awards |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Pepe is a professor of biostatistics at the University of Washington School of Public Health.<ref name=":0" /> She is a researcher at the [[Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center]].<ref name=":0" />
